chunks.arabic_text: ٢ - عَلِيّ بْن مَيْمُون، أَبُو الْحَسَن، لَقَبُهُ: أَبُو الْأَكْرَد، الصَّائِغ، كُوفِيّ.

translations.en: 2 – Ali ibn Maymun, Abu al-Hasan, his laqab is Abu al-Akrad, al-Sa'igh (the jeweler), Kufan.

chunks.arabic_text: حَدِيثُهُ يُعْرَف وَيُنْكَر، وَيُجَازُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَام).

translations.en: His hadith are recognized and denied. It is permissible to bring him out as a witness. He narrated from Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* characterizes ʿAlī ibn Maymūn as a Kufan jeweler whose hadiths are subject to *al-jarḥ wa al-taʿdīl* (criticism and validation), rendering him suitable primarily as a supporting witness (*shahid*) rather than an independent source. His transmission from Imams al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq highlights the importance of nuanced evaluation in Shia hadith sciences, where a narrator's reliability can vary depending on the context of the report.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Maymun and what is his status in hadith sciences?
